::: {#sol-reverse-sum}

We check the two hypotheses of @thm-loop-invariant.

**Initialization.**
At the first test, $i = 1$ and $j = n$, so $i + j = n + 1$.

**Maintenance.**
Suppose $i + j = n + 1$ and the guard $i < j$ are true at a test.
The swap does not change `i` or `j`,
and the body then replaces `i` with $i + 1$ and `j` with $j - 1$.
At the next test,

$$
\ba
(i + 1) + (j - 1)
&= i + j
\\&= n + 1.
\ea
$$

So, by @thm-loop-invariant, $i + j = n + 1$ is a loop invariant.

:::
